cards.prompt:
Use case: compositing / product-mockup. Asset type: one premium Mac App Store-style feature illustration, landscape 3:2, large crisp bitmap suitable for a product gallery and marketing post. Design a finished commercial artwork, not a wireframe. Visual system: confident Swiss-style sans-serif headline, sharp edges, generous spacing, graphite #151923, warm ivory #f7f5ef, rich cobalt #254dde. A broad simple colored plane and restrained soft shadows give depth; no noisy textures, generic gradients or tiny decorative clutter. Put a small app name at the top, a very large two-to-three-line headline, and a single short supporting line. Make the actual app interface the main visual subject, enlarged with a restrained dimensional tilt or carefully framed close-up. Preserve the reference app’s actual controls, proportions, icon and legible main labels. Use exact screenshot regions as the basis rather than inventing interface. Minor body text may be unobtrusive linework. This is clearly an illustrated product composition, not a raw screenshot.
Common constraints: no computer or phone hardware, people, fake reviews, ratings, metrics, awards, prices, Apple logos, App Store badges, extra brand marks or watermarks. No fictional features or controls. Never show a credential. Keep all headline text inside safe margins and spell it exactly. Remove capture cursor and purple sharing overlay. Do not include any private file names.
Inputs: image 1 is the real Settings window; image 2 is the production recording capsule on a dark canvas; image 3 is the actual icon. Use the window as an accurately cropped supporting layer, with the black capsule floating in front. Crop away the API section so the hold shortcut controls are emphasized. The capsule must retain its short pill silhouette, white mic, waveform bars and cancel X; it must not become a giant toolbar. Composition: ivory ground, large black headline on the upper left, blue plane across the lower right behind the app layers. Exact text outside UI: "Speaklet"; "Hold a key.\nSay it.\nKeep going."; "Voice to text, with a tiny control." Show the actual app icon subtly beside the name. Keep the screenshot and capsule very crisp, mostly front-facing.
refinements: Edit this artwork. Change only one thing: remove the purple macOS screen-sharing badge from the top-left corner of the Settings window. It is a capture overlay, not part of Speaklet. Restore clean blank pale title-bar background in its place. Keep every other element, text, layout, color, icon, capsule, dimensions and detail exactly unchanged.
